faqs.q: Which standards does the Steel BSPP Male × ORB Adjustable Branch Tee follow?
faqs.a: The Steel BSPP Male × ORB Adjustable Branch Tee is listed to ISO 228-1, SAE J1926, ISO 11926. ISO 228-1 covers pipe threads where pressure-tight joints are not made on the threads (the parallel G thread, for example BSPP), so the joint is sealed by a washer, O-ring or cone seat. SAE J1926 and ISO 11926 cover straight-thread O-ring ports and stud ends, the ORB type, sealed by an O-ring rather than by the thread. No test certificate is attached to the listing; tell us the documents your inspection or project needs when you ask for a quotation.

Each end mates with a part of the same thread and the same seat. The [ORB Adapters](/c/orb-adapters) range lists the matching family for the other side.

faqs.q: How do I fit the Steel BSPP Male × ORB Adjustable Branch Tee so it does not leak?
faqs.a: Match the thread and the seat before you tighten the Steel BSPP Male × ORB Adjustable Branch Tee. On a BSP parallel (BSPP) end the bonded seal, O-ring or cone seat does the sealing, not the thread, so seat the seal square and do not rely on tape to stop a leak. Clean the port first and never force a joint that does not start by hand. See our [guide to a cross-threaded port](/blog/cross-threaded-hydraulic-port) for more.

faqs.q: What is the difference between the Steel BSPP Male × ORB Adjustable Branch Tee and the Steel BSPP Male × ORB Adjustable Run Tee?

The first is marked by branch, the second by run. Choose by the thread and seat at each port you are connecting, not by the name, because adapters with similar names can have different ends.
